newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian, American end successful spacewalk.
newsitem.headline: Russian, American end successful spacewalk.

text.p: A Russian cosmonaut and a U.S. astronaut spent nearly five hours collecting dust in outer space on Tuesday before returning to the Mir orbiting station, a mission control spokesman said.
"They managed to finish their work early and so they returned ahead of schedule," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone from the control centre in the town of Korolyov, outside Moscow.

He said Vasiliy Tsibliev and NASA astronaut Jerry Linenger successfully completed the space walk at 2.08 p.m. Moscow time (1008 GMT), spending four hours and 57 minutes in space instead of about six hours initially planned.
"They closed the hatch minutes ago and now are checking the pressure in ther Mir station," the spokesman said.

The cosmonauts had to dismantle equipment which collected samples of space dust outside the station. The equipment was installed a year ago and it will be brought back to Earth by the U.S. shuttle spacecraft Atlantis next month.
The spacewalk was being videotaped from inside Mir by third crew member Alexander Lazutkin.

The Mir crew have faced several problems in the last few weeks onboard the ageing station, which has been in orbit for 11 years, including leaks in the cooling system and the latest of four small fires last February.
Toilet tanks overflowed last year after delays in bringing supplies to the station and a new generator was hastily flown to Mir after problems with energy supplies.
